column1: # Command options of P/02. The installer has no daemon or HTTP door of its own.
# Same columns as P/01: commands are the command ids in operator-commands.tsv, not HTTP routes or daemon roles.
# This table is the source of the option names, value types, defaults and conditions. Positional arguments are in operator-commands.tsv.
# type: string (a string), number (a finite decimal number), file (a file path), bool (no value).
# required and bad are CEL over f: map<string,dyn>, cmd: string; f contains supplied options, numbers as numbers, bool as true.
# - means no default. There is no implicit CLI spelling rule inherited from P/01. An option out of this form is the refusal command_options of refusals.tsv (code 2, before any effect).
# high/low and retention options carry the numeric values of their owner rows; the readers' unreadable-value rules are not new CLI refusals.
